#ifndef AEAD_WRAPPER_H
#define AEAD_WRAPPER_H

/*
 * AEAD wrapper kernel interface.
 *
 * Do not change the name or signature of aead_encrypt_call: it is the
 * pinned entry point for this kernel.
 */

int aead_encrypt_call(const unsigned char *key,
                       const unsigned char *plaintext,
                       unsigned int plaintext_len,
                       unsigned char *ciphertext_out,
                       unsigned char *tag_out);

/*
 * Internal AES-style block primitive used by aead_encrypt_call.
 * Encrypts a single 16-byte block (nonce_block) under the given
 * 16-byte key, writing 16 bytes of output to out_block.
 */
void aes_encrypt_block(const unsigned char *key,
                        const unsigned char *nonce_block,
                        unsigned char *out_block);

#endif /* AEAD_WRAPPER_H */

manifest.purpose: Hardened implementation of int aead_encrypt_call(const unsigned char *key, const unsigned char *plaintext, unsigned int plaintext_len, unsigned char *ciphertext_out, unsigned char *tag_out), signature and #include "aead_wrapper.h" unchanged. Keeps a static unsigned int counter initialized via #ifndef AEAD_TEST_COUNTER_START / #define AEAD_TEST_COUNTER_START 0u exactly as in baseline, plus a static bool exhausted flag (starts false). On entry: if exhausted is true, or if counter == 0xFFFFFFFFu AND this counter value was already consumed by a prior successful call (tracked via a static bool 'counter_in_use_since_max' set once a call succeeds with counter==0xFFFFFFFF), return -1 immediately without touching ciphertext_out/tag_out. Concretely: before doing any work, check if counter has reached 0xFFFFFFFFu and already been used once (a static bool 'have_used_max' persists this) -- if so set exhausted=true and return -1 with zero side effects. Otherwise proceed: build nonce_block from kBaseNonce (identical 12-byte constant {0x4e,0x6f,0x6e,0x63,0x65,0x42,0x61,0x73,0x65,0x30,0x30,0x31}) concatenated with big-endian counter bytes, run the same CTR-style keystream loop and tag derivation using aes_encrypt_block (identical kMixTable 256-byte S-box and round structure copied verbatim from baseline for output compatibility), write ciphertext_out/tag_out, then if counter==0xFFFFFFFFu set have_used_max=true else counter++ . This guarantees identical outputs to baseline for all pre-wraparound calls (FR1/FR2/FR4, SR1) while refusing all writes and using -1 for wraparound calls and all subsequent calls (SR2/SR3). aes_encrypt_block body must be byte-for-byte identical to inputs/aead_wrapper.cpp baseline so pre-exhaustion ciphertext/tag outputs match the reference exactly.

Unchanged copy of inputs/aead_wrapper.h: declares int aead_encrypt_call(const unsigned char*, const unsigned char*, unsigned int, unsigned char*, unsigned char*) and void aes_encrypt_block(const unsigned char*, const unsigned char*, unsigned char*) with identical include guard AEAD_WRAPPER_H. Provided so the golden .cpp compiles standalone against its own header; content is a verbatim mirror of the shipped baseline header since the interface must not change.
